title: Politics
subtitle: vote, in power, policy
summary: Talk about elections, governments and political parties, and describe the policies a party promises.

lesson.heading: Voting
lesson.text: When you **vote for** someone, you choose them by putting a cross on an official piece of paper. This is called a **secret ballot**, because no one knows who you vote for. To **elect** someone is to choose them by voting.

examples.text: I **voted for** the Green party at the last election.
It is a **secret ballot**, so no one knows who you **vote for**.
They **elected** her with a very large number of votes.
Have they set the date for the **election**?

lesson.heading: Elections in the UK
lesson.text: A **general election** is when the people elect the next **government**, the group of people who control the country. Elections are **held** at least every five years. Each **constituency** elects one person from one **political party**. That person becomes the **MP** (Member of Parliament) for that area.

examples.note: a constituency = an area where people vote

examples.text: The party with the most **MPs** forms the next **government**.
The **leader** of the party **in power** is the **Prime Minister**.
examples.note: leader = the person in control; in power = in control of the country

lesson.heading: Word families
lesson.note: Employment is an important **political** issue. The president is a very **powerful** man. I hope there will be a **reduction** in my tax.

lesson.heading: Policies
lesson.text: People usually vote for a party because they **believe in** the party's ideas. These ideas become **policies** - sets of plans and ideas that a political party has agreed on.

examples.text: My political **beliefs** are important to me.
I **believe in** free education for everyone.
Their **policy** on transport won them a lot of votes.

lesson.heading: Words in party promises
rows: We will **provide** free nursery education for all children.
provide = give something to those who need it; also provide someone with something
We will provide more **care** and **support** for **elderly** people.
care = looking after people; support = help, sometimes money; elderly = old
We will create a **fair tax** system.
fair = dealing with everyone in the same way (opp unfair); tax = money people must pay the government
above all = most importantly; treat = deal with someone in a particular way; equal = having the same importance (adv equally)

lesson.text: Use the right preposition: you **vote for** a person or a party, and you **believe in** an idea.

exercises.prompt: Have they set the date for the ___ yet?
exercises.explanation: The noun from elect is election.
The adjective from politics is political.

exercises.prompt: My political ___ are important to me.
exercises.explanation: The noun from believe is belief; the plural is beliefs.

exercises.prompt: The president is a very ___ man.
exercises.explanation: The adjective from power is powerful.

exercises.prompt: I hope there will be a ___ in my tax next year.
exercises.explanation: The noun from reduce is reduction.

exercises.prompt: Match each definition with the right word.

pairs.left: the person in control of a political party
money people must pay the government
help, often in the form of money

exercises.prompt: Which word is a synonym for 'reduce'?
exercises.explanation: Reduce = make less; the synonym is cut.

exercises.prompt: They are in control of the country. = They are in ___.
exercises.explanation: The party in power controls the country.

exercises.prompt: Elections take place every five years. = Elections are ___ every five years.
No one knows who you vote for, because it is a secret ___.
exercises.explanation: A secret ballot means nobody knows how you voted.

exercises.prompt: In Canada the country is divided into 308 political areas, though they are called 'ridings'. In the UK these areas are called ___.
exercises.explanation: A constituency is an area where people vote.

exercises.statement: The party that wins the most seats forms the next government, and the leader of that party becomes Prime Minister.
exercises.explanation: Correct. The leader of the party in power is the Prime Minister.

exercises.prompt: Put the party promise in order.
exercises.answer: We will provide more care for elderly people.
exercises.explanation: Provide = give something to those who need it; elderly = old.
